evidence: TOC-Bench provides the real-video temporal object consistency diagnostic and current Phase 0 asset source.
ScaleLong operationalizes same-content questions at four temporal scales.
Video ReCap and Ego4D-HCap provide a three-level clip-segment-video caption hierarchy.
VidSitu supplies the event-semantic middle layer through roles, coreference, and relations.
VidOSC provides explicit initial-transitioning-end temporal state intervals.
CaptainCook4D provides real procedural steps and induced errors.
PIE-V provides structured mistake injection and recovery correction traces.
Same-video Clip/Shot/Event/Story questions partially address cross-scale comparability, but not structural links.
Clip, segment, and video captions partially instantiate a semantic hierarchy.
Entity coreference connects participants across event intervals, but only in short clips.
Object-track grounded construction targets identity persistence, although full tracks are not part of the public QA schema.
Initial/transitioning/end intervals support state localization but not executable operators.
Normal and induced-error procedures provide error supervision without systematic recovery targets.
PIE-V explicitly generates error and recovery correction traces with coherence rubrics.
The proposed data contract makes same-video cross-level structural links mandatory.
The proposed task requires legal corruptions, repair targets, and post-repair consistency proofs.
Persistent identity anchors are linked to state, event roles, and episode references.
T-STEP-v0 ledger-core supplies the candidate typed executable semantics.
R2 tests whether a contract-fixed local ledger core is supportable on new immutable TOC-Bench real-video samples.
The experiment uses ten all-new TOC-Bench videos and finds 6/10 strict contract compatibility, so TOC-Bench remains a diagnostic rather than sole supervision source.
